newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Worries that the U.S. Federal Reserve Board may increase interest rates prompted investors to sell some large capitalised stocks, take profits and drive down the index on Tuesday, brokers said.

"Some investors are reluctant to invest as they believe the Fed would hike its rates by 25 basis points when it meets later today. They are also waiting for key economic indicators to be released by the Thai central bank on Thursday," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of SITCA Investment and Securities.
The SET composite index fell 3.17 points to 710.68 on 2.4 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index slipped 0.36 point to 52.92.
Advancers led decliners 180 to 113 while 103 issues remained unchanged.
"Investors sold large capitalised stocks such as TelecomAsia and Siam Cement and took profits today. Foreigners are believed to continue buying from yesterday," Somchai said.
TelecomAsia was ranked sixth on the list of most active stocks in terms of value, falling 0.50 baht to 44, while Siam Cement retreated 16 to 628.
Large capitalised banking and finance issues dominated the list of most active stocks in terms of value.
Thai Farmers Bank was first-ranked on the list, unchanged at 120 baht. Krung Thai Bank gained 0.25 to 36.25.
In the finance sector, General Finance and Securities rose 0.75 to 17.75 and Dhana Siam Finance advanced one to 36.50.
